ruling.recommended_action: Close the dispute as no_action: the sole off-route segment (F3) was covered by the rider's pre-segment general route authorisation, so no route refund is due; no account flag.
ruling.reasoning:
The trip was a RydeTAXI metered trip (F7), so RD-2's metered branch applies: any unexempted off-route segment's extra_km is refunded at this trip's per-km rate, distance fare ÷ distance km [F4][RD-2]. RD-1 is satisfied because one off-route segment exists: F3 records 13:07–13:19, 7.41 km driven where the optimal route covers 2.38 km, +5.03 km, up to 1391 m off route [F3][RD-1]. The whole case therefore turns on RD-5 for that single segment.

RD-5 requires a rider's own message sent before the segment start, agreeing to the route, and the agreement must cover that segment [F9][RD-5]. The driver asked at 13:03, "shall I take another way?" [F8], and the rider replied at 13:04, "Just take whichever way is faster lah, I'm late." [F9]. Both chat messages are timestamped and the record is complete [F10], so the consent is rider-issued and precedes the 13:07 segment start by three minutes [F9][F10][RD-5]. The driver's statement F11 is not consent and I do not rely on it [F11][RD-5].

On scope, "Just take whichever way is faster" is a general route choice, not a named road [F9][RD-5]. A general authorisation covers the route chosen to reach the destination and excludes only the driver's own business — a stop away from the route or a loop that reaches nothing [F9][RD-5]. F3 shows no stop at all and no errand: the car kept moving on a driving route toward Suntec City, which is consistent with the driver routing around the Ayer Rajah Expressway queue he had flagged [F3][F8]. Nothing in the record places this segment on a wrong errand, so the general consent covers it, and the segment is exempt under RD-5. RD-3 is not engaged because no rider-named stop appears and no stop was measured in the segment [F3][F9][RD-3(a)]. RD-4 is unavailable: no qualifying incident exists [F15], and the Ayer Rajah Expressway band-2 record cannot exempt on its own [F12][RD-4].

Because the only segment is exempt, the route-related refund is zero and the metered fare of $60.30, including the excess-distance and waiting items, stays as charged [F4][F5][F7][RD-2]. Had the segment counted, the figure would have been 5.03 km × ($42.36 ÷ 30.04 km = $1.4101/km) = $7.09 [F4][F7][RD-2] — but that arithmetic only applies to an unexempted segment, and this one is exempt. No account flag: the trace marks the RD-6 precondition failed, with route_disputes_upheld_90d = 0 [F18][RD-6].

segment_findings.reason: Rider message F9 at 13:04, before the 13:07 segment start in F3, answered the driver's 13:03 question F8 with 'Just take whichever way is faster lah, I'm late.' — a general route choice for reaching Suntec City [F9][RD-5]. F3 records no stop and no errand; the car kept moving on a driving route, so the general authorisation covers this segment [F3][F8][RD-5]. Driver statement F11 is not rider-issued consent and is not relied on [F11][RD-5].

rejected_claims.reason: The +5.6 km aggregate and the $7.88 billed excess [F1][F4] are accepted as arithmetic, but RD-2 refunds only the extra_km of an unexempted segment [RD-2]; the sole segment F3 is exempt under RD-5 on the rider's own pre-segment message F9, so no amount is refundable.

The segment's existence and measurements in F3 are accepted [F3][RD-1], but the claim that it is unexempted fails: the rider agreed before the segment to 'whichever way is faster' [F9][RD-5], which covers a route chosen to get to the destination, and F3 shows no stop or driver errand.

Correctly read as a general route consent [F9][RD-5], but a general authorisation is not limited to a named road and is not defeated by F1/F2's longer trip [F1][F2][RD-5]; the limitation the clause attaches is a driver's own errand or a loop to nowhere, and F3 shows neither.
Agreed that F11 is a post-trip statement and not consent [F11][RD-5]; that does not matter because the consent relied on is the rider's own timestamped message F9, sent before the segment.

Accepted that RD-4(a) is unavailable on F15 and that the band-2 record F12 cannot exempt alone under RD-4(b) [F15][F12][RD-4]; the exemption here comes from RD-5 consent, not from the traffic branch, so the point does not decide the case.

F2 and F16 are accurate [F2][F16], but RD-5's test is whether the rider agreed to the route before the segment, not whether the authorised route proved faster; a general authorisation that turns out slower is still an authorisation, and the excess-duration point is not a ground of recovery under RD-2.

The formula 5.03 km × ($42.36 ÷ 30.04 km = $1.4101/km) = $7.09 is the correct RD-2 measure [F4][F7][RD-2], but it is payable only if the segment is unexempted; F3 is exempt under RD-5, so the amount is zero.
Conceded by both sides and confirmed by the trace: route_disputes_upheld_90d = 0 in F18 fails the RD-6 precondition, so no flag_account [F18][RD-6].
Reading F8, F9 and F11 in context, no threat, intimidation, harassment, sexual remark or dangerous-driving allegation appears [F8][F9][F11][SAFE-1]; the screen is recorded as none.

The $7.09 figure D5 offers as the correct measure [F4][F5][RD-2] is not adopted as a payable amount: the segment is exempt, so the trace formula yields zero and the $0.11 waiting item stands separately as metered waiting time on a RydeTAXI trip [F5][RD-3].

The submission that the 5.03 km excess 'exceeds' the extra duration [F2][F12] is a comparison argument, not a ground of exemption; the general consent in F9 [RD-5] is what exempts the segment, and it does so without any finding about which road was faster.
